articleTitle: Proving the design in the safety case
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Designing Safety-Critical Systems
abstract: It is becoming increasingly common to require a safety case to be provided for a safety-critical system prior to its deployment. This paper discusses some work under way to provide an effective way of structuring the safety case, and relating the emerging design to the safety analysis. It proposes a new way of organising and structuring development and assessment processes to encourage the stronger integration of design and analysis. Part of the aim is to facilitate change management. A 'top down' development model is assumed, and the need for investigating different designs, including assessing different design strategies for their safety properties, is recognised. The key concepts of goal structures constituting the basis of the process model are reviewed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ensuring public safety in PLC controlled water treatment plants
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Designing Safety-Critical Systems
abstract: Design methods are outlined which are thought to achieve a favourable balance between cost and risk in largely unmanned drinking-water treatment stations. A hardwired emergency shutdown system, software best practice, and telemetry to a central computing facility from more than 1500 sites are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The assessment and control of risk in the development of medical systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Designing Safety-Critical Systems
abstract: The inadequacy of the traditional approach to medical device safety assessment for increasingly complex and software-controlled systems is exposed. The process of risk analysis in the draft European standard is presented in flowchart form. A qualitative risk estimation method is adapted from a draft IEC generic standard.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Expert systems for safety-critical applications: theory, technology and applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Designing Safety-Critical Systems
abstract: A knowledge base may contain no demonstrable errors or inconsistencies, and the programs which apply it may operate as intended, yet the advice given by an expert system may be sub-optimal or even unsafe. This problem of consequential safety is an inevitable consequence of attempting to build practical technologies on the basis of some current state-of-the-art in any field which is not fully understood. This paper is concerned with issues concerning the design of such systems whose advice may have implications for safety. It sets out the objectives and formal specification methods of a Rigorously Engineered Decisions (RED) project extending and applying symbolic decision theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
